description: CAD bake-off 3 of 3 -- BLENDER: build the SO-101 gripper assembly parametrically in cad/blender/. SHARED CONTEXT (same task, three tools, one pebble each so they can run in separate git worktrees): recreate the SO-101 gripper assembly -- the fixed jaw (gripper body) and the moving jaw -- as a baseline for comparing three CAD tools. Jake verbatim: "I want to be able to modify them in the future, so you will have to do it in a way that supports that." That means parametric, editable source. Importing a mesh and calling it done FAILS the test. Use named variables for every dimension that might plausibly change: jaw length, jaw opening, fingertip thickness, servo horn bore, fastener sizes, wall thickness. DIMENSIONAL SOURCE OF TRUTH -- two real SO-101 STEP files are already committed at cad/build123d/reference/: Moving_Jaw_SO101.step and Wrist_Roll_Follower_SO101.step. STEP carries exact analytic geometry, so measure from these. Do NOT re-download them and do NOT invent or eyeball dimensions from tessellated meshes. WHY THIS PART: it is what Jake will modify for the Hand 1.0 paper gripper -- cross-reference plans/hand_1_0.md and plans/gripper_bet.md as reading, and cite them in your notes. DELIVERABLE BESIDES THE MODEL: a NOTES.md in your own tool directory covering time taken, what was easy, what was painful, whether the tool known weakness actually mattered in practice, and how it would feel to modify this part six months from now. State plainly if the geometry ends up approximate and list what still needs verifying. BOUNDARIES: stay inside your own cad/<tool>/ directory and touch nothing else. Do NOT edit plans/hand_1_0.md or plans/gripper_bet.md -- a later pass writes the comparison across all three tools. The other two tool pebbles are running in parallel in their own worktrees, so do not touch cad/openscad/, cad/build123d/, or cad/blender/ other than your own. TOOL SPECIFICS: Blender is at /Applications/Blender.app and runs headless via /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender --background --python <script>. THE CRUX FOR THIS ONE: Blender is NOT parametric CAD, so the only way to meet Jake requirement that the part stay modifiable is to build it from a bpy script with a named-parameter block at the top -- re-running the script regenerates the model. Hand-modelling a mesh and saving the .blend does not count. Deliver the bpy script, a PNG render, an STL export, and the saved .blend, all produced headlessly. Read dimensions from the reference STEP files at cad/build123d/reference/ (measure only -- write nothing into that directory; if Blender cannot read STEP directly, say so in NOTES.md and describe how you got the numbers without inventing them). VERDICT SHOULD BE EVEN-HANDED: note fairly where Blender genuinely wins -- rendering, visualization, and the fact that the existing Tool Caddy scene already lives in Blender (plans/tool-caddy.blend) -- alongside where the lack of parametric CAD and B-rep hurts.
test_instructions: cad/blender/ contains a bpy script with a named-parameter block at the top covering jaw length, jaw opening, fingertip thickness, servo horn bore, fastener sizes and wall thickness, and re-running it regenerates the model
A PNG render, an STL export and a saved .blend are committed, all produced via Blender --background --python

cad/blender/NOTES.md covers time, easy, painful, whether Blender not being parametric CAD actually mattered here, where Blender genuinely wins (rendering, visualization, existing Tool Caddy scene), six-month modifiability, and what still needs verifying
Dimensions trace back to the reference STEP files rather than being invented, and cad/build123d/reference/ is unmodified
Nothing outside cad/blender/ is modified -- in particular plans/hand_1_0.md and plans/gripper_bet.md are untouched
